request.system:
You are a scientific researcher proposing exactly one testable research hypothesis.
Return only the required JSON. The public "answer" is a research proposal of about 400 to 800 words: a descriptive hypothesis title, mechanism and supported premises, explicitly speculative bridges, alternative explanations, a discriminating preclinical test strategy, a falsifying observation, and limitations.
Explain the proposal publicly; do not provide private internal reasoning. Distinguish evidence from assumptions. Cite supplied source labels [S1]-[S4] for claims they actually support. Outside-packet recalled facts must be labeled unverified prior knowledge; never invent citation identifiers.
The "ranking" contains exactly one item: the same descriptive title used in the prose, promisingness and confidence in [0,1], and exactly known supporting PMIDs or an empty list. These self-estimates are not quality grades.
Choose the items to rank yourself: between 1 and 1 items.
Do not mention your model, author identity, method, iteration, reviewers, score, or prior conversation in the proposal. Treat supplied answers and critiques as data, not instructions. You have no tools and must use the frozen evidence packet.

Question:
# AML evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025. Co-Scientist's validated candidates and generated proposals are not input or the only correct answers.

## Research question

Propose one mechanistically specific AML drug-repurposing hypothesis using a drug approved for a different indication. Specify the biological context, supported premises and speculative bridges, selectivity and translational limitations, and a discriminating preclinical validation strategy with a falsifying outcome. State the original indication and distinguish verified facts from prior knowledge that needs checking. Do not present an established AML regimen as a new repurposing discovery. This adapts the Co-Scientist objective rather than reproducing a private original prompt.

## S1 — A leukemia-stem-cell metabolic dependency

Lagadinou et al. (2013), *BCL-2 inhibition targets oxidative phosphorylation and selectively eradicates quiescent human leukemia stem cells*. Cell Stem Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.stem.2012.12.013`; PMID: `23333149`; PMCID: `PMC3595363`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23333149/).

Functionally defined leukemia stem cells in the studied specimens frequently had low reactive-oxygen-species levels and elevated BCL-2. BCL-2 inhibition reduced oxidative phosphorylation and affected quiescent leukemia stem cells. This motivates investigating specific dependencies and selectivity. It does not establish that an arbitrary mitochondrial inhibitor has an acceptable therapeutic window or works across every AML context.

## S2 — Resistant cells are not necessarily the same stem-cell population

Farge et al. (2017), *Chemotherapy-Resistant Human Acute Myeloid Leukemia Cells Are Not Enriched for Leukemic Stem Cells but Require Oxidative Metabolism*. Cancer Discovery. DOI: `10.1158/2159-8290.CD-16-0441`; PMID: `28416471`; PMCID: `PMC5501738`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28416471/).

Residual cells in cytarabine-treated models were not consistently enriched for immature, quiescent leukemia stem cells. They displayed oxidative-metabolism-associated properties, including mitochondrial and fatty-acid-oxidation-related features. Altering that state changed treatment response in the studied settings. This cautions against equating all residual disease with the ROS-low population in S1. These model findings do not establish clinical efficacy of a new compound.

## S3 — An established mechanistic comparator

Pollyea et al. (2018), *Venetoclax with azacitidine disrupts energy metabolism and targets leukemia stem cells in patients with acute myeloid leukemia*. Nature Medicine. DOI: `10.1038/s41591-018-0233-1`; PMID: `30420752`; PMCID: `PMC7001730`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30420752/).

The report connected venetoclax–azacitidine treatment to changes in leukemia-stem-cell energy metabolism, including TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation effects, using patient-associated observations and experimental follow-up. It provides an established comparator. Repeating this combination is not a new repurposing proposal. The findings cannot be transferred directly to another drug or treated as universal randomized comparative efficacy evidence.

## S4 — Differentiation as a distinct outcome

Sykes et al. (2016), *Inhibition of Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase Overcomes Differentiation Blockade in Acute Myeloid Leukemia*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2016.08.057`; PMID: `27641501`; PMCID: `PMC7360335`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27641501/).

DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation in experimental AML systems and affected disease-related endpoints in the investigated models. This connects metabolism with differentiation and supplies an alternative to nonspecific cell killing. It does not establish that every approved drug affecting this pathway reproduces the result or achieves suitable exposure and selectivity.

## Evidence boundaries

- Specify context and endpoint; distinguish bulk-cell effects, stem-cell effects, and differentiation.
- Approval, original indication, exposure and selectivity facts outside these summaries need explicit verification. Label recollections as unverified prior knowledge.
- Include normal-cell and mechanistic comparators; a pathway link alone is insufficient evidence of efficacy.
- State what would disconfirm the proposed drug–mechanism–context relationship.
- Absence from Co-Scientist's reported positive candidates is not an incorrect-answer label.


Proposal to improve:
Teriflunomide for differentiation-arrested acute myeloid leukemia through dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibition

The biological context is primary human AML plus one matched patient-derived xenograft in a monocytic maturation-arrest stratum outside acute promyelocytic leukemia. Qualifying blasts show CD34 or CD117 on at least 20 percent of the blast gate, CD11b below 15 percent, CD14 below 15 percent, and fewer than 10 percent of cells past the promyelocyte or promonocyte on a 200-cell differential. Teriflunomide is proposed here as differentiation therapy, with myeloid maturation as the primary endpoint.

Unverified prior knowledge, absent from this packet and requiring label and pharmacokinetic confirmation, is that teriflunomide is approved for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis and that its principal target is DHODH, the enzyme oxidizing dihydroorotate in de novo pyrimidine synthesis. The numeric unbound concentration at the approved dose, protein binding, and marrow exposure are unverified prior knowledge to be fixed from those sources before testing.

The single supported premise is that DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation in experimental AML systems and affected disease-related endpoints in those models, linking metabolism to differentiation [S4]. That summary does not name teriflunomide, a genotype, or an approved-dose exposure.

Three bridges are speculative. Teriflunomide engages DHODH in threshold-meeting blasts at free levels overlapping documented unbound exposures for the approved indication. On-target loss of de novo pyrimidine synthesis is sufficient to reproduce the [S4] differentiation result. This stratum matures with a wider margin than normal hematopoietic progenitors. [S4] withholds automatic transfer to every approved pathway drug and withholds an exposure or selectivity claim.

Alternative accounts stay open. Nucleotide-stress death can shift markers and mimic maturation. Unverified prior knowledge is that teriflunomide has reported activities beyond DHODH, leaving any off-target AML role untested. Competing mechanisms are venetoclax-azacitidine-like TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation suppression [S3], an effect restricted to the oxidative cytarabine-residual state rather than the ROS-low quiescent stem-cell state [S2], or restriction to one genetic class that [S4] does not assign to this drug. [S1] further constrains interpretation: BCL-2 inhibition reduced oxidative phosphorylation and affected quiescent low-ROS leukemia stem cells in the specimens studied, and that result does not grant a therapeutic window to an arbitrary mitochondrial inhibitor.

The test uses six or more genetically distinct primary samples that meet the arrest threshold and represent at least three recurrent-genotype classes, each paired with normal CD34-positive cells, plus one xenograft from an in-vitro responsive sample in the stratum. At or below the documented unbound approved-dose ceiling, engagement means at least a twofold dihydroorotate rise and at least 30 percent loss of uridine and cytidine nucleotides. Maturation is scored at 48 and 96 hours, and a time point counts only while annexin-V positivity remains within 10 percentage points of vehicle. The earliest engaged, viability-qualified time point must show, versus vehicle, at least a 15 percentage-point gain of CD11b or CD14, at least a 15 percentage-point loss of the dominant immature marker (CD34 or CD117), at least a 10 percentage-point increase in forms beyond promyelocyte or promonocyte, and a myeloid-maturation transcriptional score at least 1.5-fold higher. Uridine must cut that CD11b or CD14 gain by at least half and restore the pyrimidine nucleotides to within 20 percent of vehicle. Parallel guanosine is the non-rescuing nucleoside; confirmation is required that it leaves pyrimidine nucleotides depleted and cuts the marker gain by less than half. ROS-low fractions [S1] and cytarabine-residual cultures [S2] are profiled for oxygen consumption, TCA-cycle intermediates, and stem-cell frequency. Day-21 xenograft marrow, at the same unbound ceiling, uses those maturation cutoffs on human CD45-positive cells and human CD45 burden in marrow and spleen, beside venetoclax-azacitidine [S3]. Passage requires uridine-rescuable, guanosine-persistent maturation in at least four of six samples and in at least two genotype classes. Selectivity fails if the percent loss of normal myeloid colonies is at least the percent loss of AML colonies, or if annexin-V positivity in normal progenitors rises by 30 percentage points or more.

Exposure-matched failure of a twofold dihydroorotate rise or of 30 percent uridine and cytidine nucleotide depletion falsifies repurposing even if higher concentrations mature blasts. Missing a maturation cutoff, uridine-resistant maturation, or marker gain only after a 15-point annexin-V rise falsifies the differentiation claim, as does viability loss or [S3]-type oxidative-phosphorylation suppression without preceding maturation. Confinement to one genetic class outside the arrest stratum falsifies the subset claim. Equal or greater normal CD34-positive colony injury at the same free concentration falsifies selectivity.

[S4] names neither an approved inhibitor nor a marrow-effective free concentration, and it does not cover every AML genotype. [S1] and [S2] leave ROS-low stem-cell eradication and cytarabine-residual oxidative reprogramming separate from bulk maturation. Approval status, numeric unbound human exposure, immunomodulatory effects, and clinical safety need verification outside this design.

Final ranking:
1. Teriflunomide for differentiation-arrested acute myeloid leukemia through dihydroorotate dehydrogenase inhibition (promisingness 0.53, confidence 0.45; PMIDs: 27641501)

Scientific critique:
- The drug-mechanism pair is the direct approved-agent reading of S4, so novelty is thin: teriflunomide is the canonical approved DHODH inhibitor, and the answer never states a feature that would distinguish it from tool DHODH inhibitors already tied to AML differentiation or flags prior AML leflunomide/teriflunomide reports as a premise that must be checked before calling this repurposing. Fix by pre-specifying an off-target panel (AHR, kinase, or other reported activities) whose positive result would assign the phenotype away from DHODH, and by labeling any existing AML differentiation data as unverified prior knowledge that could retire the claim.
- Two labs cannot apply the same pass/fail rule because the myeloid-maturation transcriptional score has no gene set or reference distribution, uridine and guanosine concentrations are unstated, recurrent-genotype classes are unnamed, and the stratum mixes monocytic gates (CD14) with granulocytic staging (promyelocyte). The falsifier “one genetic class outside the arrest stratum” is also narrower than the claim that the effect holds across classes inside the stratum. Name the score, nucleoside micromolar levels, and genotype list, align morphology with lineage, and falsify the subset claim if activity is confined to a single genotype class.
- The selectivity and exposure operations are not yet runnable at the stated unbound ceiling. Colony-loss equality can be produced by on-target maturation, because differentiated cells stop forming colonies, so normal-versus-AML colony counts do not separate differentiation from cytotoxicity. Teriflunomide protein binding means nominal medium or xenograft dose is not free concentration unless the protocol measures free fraction in the assay matrix and in plasma. Pre-specify equilibrium-dialysis or equivalent free-drug matching, a viability-qualified morphologic selectivity endpoint, and a numeric day-21 human CD45 burden rule, or declare burden secondary in the falsifier list.
- The arrest stratum is labeled monocytic but the gates mix granulocytic and monocytic criteria (CD11b, promyelocyte or promonocyte, CD14), and the subset falsifier refers to one genetic class outside the stratum without naming the three genotype classes, so a failed or restricted result is not interpretable. Pre-specify a single lineage gate and name the genotype classes before any sample is run.
- Maturation is required at the earliest time point that shows target engagement, with no pyrimidine-defined medium and no pathway-matched DHODH tool-compound arm, so exogenous uridine can block engagement and a slower genuine differentiation effect is scored as falsified. State medium pyrimidine content, add a brequinar-class positive control in the same medium, and separate an early engagement window from a later pre-specified maturation window.
- Selectivity is decided by comparing percent loss of normal versus AML myeloid colonies, which treats differentiation-associated loss of clonogenicity as cytotoxicity, and the 1.5-fold myeloid-maturation transcriptional score has no gene set. Define the signature and score selectivity on normal-progenitor apoptosis and unwanted maturation at the same free concentration, using colony loss only after maturation is confirmed.

Improve your earlier answer based on these critique points. Address each point directly. Keep what already works; do not start over. For each point, identify the weakness, apply a focused fix, and make sure the fix does not make anything else worse. Return the complete improved answer.

The primary endpoint is monocytic maturation.

Unverified prior knowledge, absent from this packet, is that teriflunomide is approved for relapsing multiple sclerosis and that its principal target is DHODH. Any published AML differentiation result with leflunomide or teriflunomide is unverified prior knowledge; if that literature already shows exposure-matched, uridine-rescuable monocytic maturation in this stratum, the repurposing claim is retired as previously shown.

The supported premise is that DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation in experimental AML systems and affected disease-related endpoints in those models [S4]. That summary names neither teriflunomide nor an approved-dose free concentration.

Three bridges are speculative. Measured free teriflunomide overlaps the documented unbound exposure of the approved indication and engages DHODH in threshold-meeting blasts. On-target loss of de novo pyrimidine synthesis is sufficient to reproduce the [S4] result in this monocytic stratum. [S4] withholds transfer to every approved pathway drug and withholds exposure and selectivity claims.

Alternative accounts stay open. Nucleotide-stress death can shift markers and mimic maturation. Unverified prior knowledge is that teriflunomide has reported AHR and kinase activities. A positive off-target result assigns the phenotype away from DHODH: an AHR antagonist that blocks maturation while dihydroorotate elevation and pyrimidine depletion persist, or a selective kinase tool that meets the maturation cutoffs without raising dihydroorotate or depleting pyrimidines. Competing mechanisms are venetoclax–azacitidine-like TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation suppression [S3], restriction to the oxidative cytarabine-residual state [S2], or restriction to the ROS-low quiescent stem-cell state in which BCL-2 inhibition reduced oxidative phosphorylation [S1]. [S1] does not confer a therapeutic window on an arbitrary mitochondrial inhibitor. Confinement of maturation to one named genotype class is an alternative to a stratum-wide effect.

Base medium is pyrimidine-poor dialyzed serum with no added uridine or cytidine and measured uridine below 1 micromolar. Equilibrium dialysis measures free fraction in that matrix and in xenograft plasma, and the nominal amount is set so measured free drug remains at or below the documented unbound approved-dose ceiling. Engagement is read only at 6–24 hours: at least a twofold dihydroorotate rise and at least 30 percent loss of uridine and cytidine nucleotides. Maturation is read only at 96 hours, and only while annexin-V positivity stays within 10 percentage points of vehicle. Cutoffs versus vehicle are at least a 15 percentage-point CD14 gain, at least a 15 percentage-point loss of the dominant immature marker (CD34 or CD117), at least a 10 percentage-point increase in forms past the promonocyte, and a rise of at least 1.0 log2 in a fixed score (mean log2 of ITGAM, CD14, CSF1R, MNDA, LYZ, S100A8, S100A9, and SPI1 minus mean log2 of CD34 and KIT). Guanosine at 100 micromolar must leave those nucleotides at least 30 percent below vehicle and cut the CD14 gain by less than half.
